expectations.text: Report identifies that the plan specifies rate limiting by IP address but the code uses session IDs
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Critical Semantic Mismatch: IP addresses vs. Session IDs — The plan is unambiguous: every feature is defined in terms of IP addresses' and 'The plan specifies IP-based rate limiting; the implementation uses session IDs throughout.'

expectations.text: Report notes that method signatures use session_id parameter where the plan specifies ip_address
expectations.evidence: Report provides a table with all mismatches: 'check_rate_limit(ip_address) | check_rate_limit(session_id)', 'record_request(ip_address) | record_request(session_id)', etc.

expectations.text: Report flags that check_rate_limit, record_request, and get_remaining all accept session_id instead of ip_address
expectations.evidence: Report table explicitly lists check_rate_limit, record_request, and get_remaining as using session_id instead of ip_address with FAIL status for each.

expectations.text: Report flags that allowlist operations use session_id instead of ip_address
expectations.evidence: Report table shows is_allowlisted, add_to_allowlist, remove_from_allowlist all as FAIL with 'Signature uses session_id, not ip_address'.

expectations.text: Report confirms all tests pass despite the semantic mismatch
expectations.evidence: Report states: '8 passed in 0.01s — All 8 tests pass. No failures, no errors.' and 'The implementation is functionally coherent and all tests pass.'

expectations.text: Report does NOT simply claim the plan is fully implemented just because tests pass
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Overall verdict: FAIL — Tests pass but the implementation does not match the plan. The plan specifies IP-based rate limiting; the implementation uses session IDs throughout.'

expectations.text: Report identifies that get_top_offenders returns session IDs not IP addresses as the plan requires
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'get_top_offenders(n) returns IPs sorted by request count | FAIL | Returns session IDs; no IP-address semantics' and 'get_top_offenders(n) returns session IDs sorted by count'.

expectations.text: Report classifies this as a semantic deviation, not just a naming difference — the tracking dimension (IP vs session) changes the security behavior
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Session IDs are typically application-layer tokens, while IP addresses are network-layer identifiers. A session ID rate limiter does not protect against abuse from a single IP that spawns multiple sessions, which is the core threat model the plan is designed to address.'

claims.claim: Tests were written to match the incorrect implementation rather than to validate plan requirements
claims.evidence: Report states: 'The tests were written to match the (incorrect) implementation rather than to validate the plan's requirements, which is why they all pass despite the implementation being wrong.'
Report states: '_get_session_id(self, request_context) (line 12–13) is defined but never called anywhere in the class or tests. It appears to be dead code left over from a different design.'

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions, evals look solid. Both reports correctly identified all key aspects of this scenario.
